name: Breadboard (830 points)
desc: A board full of holes for building circuits without soldering. Parts and wires just push in.

name: Jumper Wires (M-M, M-F, F-F)
desc: Pre-made wires with pins or sockets on the ends. Male-to-male for the breadboard, female ends for module pins.

name: Resistor Kit (220Ω–10kΩ)
desc: An assortment of common resistors: 100Ω, 220Ω, 330Ω, 1kΩ, 2kΩ, 4.7kΩ and 10kΩ. They limit current for LEDs and make pull-ups and voltage dividers.
note: Read values with the color bands or, easier, a multimeter.

name: USB Data Cable (for your board)
desc: Connects your board to the PC for uploading code and power. Match the plug: USB-B (Uno/Mega), Mini-B or USB-C (Nano), Micro-B or USB-C (ESP32/Pico).
note: Classic trap: some cables are charge-only and carry no data. If the PC doesn't see your board, try another cable first.

name: Ceramic Capacitors 100nF (0.1µF)
desc: Tiny capacitors (marked "104") that smooth out electrical noise. Used for decoupling and to stop buttons from "bouncing".

name: Electrolytic Capacitor Kit (1µF–1000µF)
desc: Can-shaped capacitors that store a bit of energy and steady the power supply. LED strips and radios love them.
note: Polarity matters: the stripe marks the − leg. Backwards or over-voltage, they can pop.

name: 1N4007 Diodes
desc: One-way valves for electricity. Placed backwards across a motor or relay coil, it soaks up the voltage spike when it switches off (a "flyback diode").
note: The silver stripe is the cathode (−) end. For a flyback diode, the stripe faces the + supply.

name: NPN Transistors (PN2222A / 2N2222)
desc: A small electronic switch: a weak pin current turns on a bigger current (up to ~500mA). Use it for buzzers, small motors and relays.
note: The pin order DIFFERS between makers: PN2222A is often E-B-C and P2N2222A is C-B-E. Check the datasheet for the exact marking on yours.

name: IRLZ44N Logic-Level MOSFET
desc: A heavy-duty electronic switch that lets a 5V pin control big loads like LED strips, pumps and motors (several amps).
voltage: Up to 55V · fully on with a 5V gate
note: Pins: Gate, Drain, Source (left to right, facing the label). Add a 10kΩ resistor from gate to GND.

warn.3.3: From a 3.3V pin the IRLZ44N only partly turns on: fine for loads under ~1A, but it can get hot with big motors.

name: Logic Level Shifter (4-ch, BSS138)
desc: A tiny translator between 3.3V and 5V signals, so a 3.3V board (ESP32/Pico) can safely talk to 5V modules.
note: Connect LV to 3.3V, HV to 5V, and both GNDs. Not fast enough for WS2812B strips (use a 74AHCT125 for those).
